title: Reference-Count Decrement Returning a Should-Free Flag to the Caller
pattern: A hand-rolled reference-count release decrements the count and returns a boolean telling the caller to destroy the object, instead of performing the release itself.
why_bad: Correct destruction depends on every call site checking and acting on the flag. A caller that ignores it leaks the object; one that frees on the wrong condition, or after another thread has taken a new reference, causes use-after-free or double free.
detection: A method that decrements a reference or usage count and returns `bool` (or the new count) that callers compare against zero to decide whether to free, drop or recycle the object, with no release callback or `Drop` implementation doing it.
counterexample: `Arc`/`Rc` and other types that release in `Drop`; kernel-style `kref_put(&kref, release_fn)` APIs that take the release function and invoke it themselves; lock-free algorithms where the return value is consumed by the same primitive that performs reclamation.
source: Paul E. McKenney, *Is Parallel Programming Hard, And, If So, What Can You Do About It?* (2020), Ch. 13 "Reference Counting".
